name: Kachari Ruins (Ruins of Kachari Rajbari)
description: Medieval ruins of the ancient Dimasa Kachari kingdom capital in Dimapur, featuring distinctive mushroom-domed sandstone pillars (8–15 feet high) elaborately carved with animals, birds, flowers and motifs. Dating to the 10th–13th centuries, the site was the kingdom’s seat before the Ahom invasion; protected by the Archaeological Survey of India and one of Nagaland’s most distinctive archaeological landmarks.
facts: Ancient capital of the Dimasa Kachari kingdom
Mushroom-domed carved sandstone pillars
Dates to 10th–13th centuries
ASI protected monument
Located near Circuit House and Naga Shopping Arcade

name: Dimapur
description: Largest city and commercial capital of Nagaland, situated on the banks of the Dhansiri River. Serves as the primary gateway to the state via its airport and major railway station; a bustling urban centre blending Naga culture, markets, historical sites and modern amenities.
facts: Largest city and main commercial hub of Nagaland
Elevation around 145 m
Key entry point via Dimapur Airport (DMU) and railway station
On the banks of the Dhansiri River
Gateway to Kohima (about 75 km) and the rest of Nagaland

name: Nagaland Science Centre
description: Interactive science museum and educational centre in Dimapur with galleries on senses, fun science and a children’s corner, plus a planetarium (Taramandal). Established to promote scientific awareness among students and the public through hands-on exhibits.
facts: Inaugurated December 2004
Located on Super Market Lane, Half Nagarjan
Features interactive exhibits and planetarium
Open 10 AM–4 PM, closed Mondays
Entry fee nominal; ideal for families and students

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Dimapur’s best-known and busiest market, famous for affordable clothing, footwear, electronics, jewellery and imported goods from Myanmar, Thailand and China. A vibrant commercial and cultural hub where locals and visitors bargain and experience everyday Naga urban life.
facts: Central market popular for bargains on imported goods
Clothing, electronics, jewellery and daily essentials
Busy commercial heart of Dimapur
Popular with both locals and tourists
Easy access by local transport

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and North East Heritage Museum
description: Cultural complex of the North East Zone Cultural Centre featuring a stone sculpture garden with works by artists from across India, traditional morungs, amphitheatre and a museum showcasing crafts and artefacts from the eight northeastern states.
facts: Located near Dimapur airport and railway station
Stone sculpture garden with 31 works
North East Heritage Museum of regional crafts
Official district places-of-interest listing
Promotes cultural heritage of the Northeast

name: Green Park
description: Landscaped recreational park inside the State Horticulture Nursery at 4th Mile, Dimapur. Offers greenery, boating, picnic areas, water zorbing, ziplining and children’s activities; a popular local getaway for families.
facts: Located at 4th Mile within State Horticulture Nursery
Boating, ziplining, water zorbing and kids’ activities
Nominal entry fee; open mainly weekends and holidays
Official district tourist place
Popular for picnics and short family outings

name: Longwa Village (Lungwa)
description: Unique Konyak Naga village in Mon district that straddles the India-Myanmar international border. The Angh’s (chief’s) house sits directly on the border line, allowing visitors to stand in two countries at once. Known for traditional Konyak culture, last remaining face-tattooed headhunters, wooden architecture, and remote border location.
facts: Village and Angh’s house straddle India-Myanmar border
Home of Konyak tribe with headhunting heritage
Visitors can stand in two countries without visa
Approx 35-42 km from Mon town
Famous for dual-citizenship experience for residents

name: Shangnyu Village
description: Prominent Konyak village near Mon town featuring a 500-year-old Angh’s house with traditional wooden carvings, memorial stones, and fertility symbols. Offers insight into ancient Konyak craftsmanship, warrior history, and living tribal architecture.
facts: 500-year-old Angh’s palace with unique carvings
Memorial stones in front of the chief’s house
About 6-9 km from Mon town
Stronghold of traditional Konyak culture
Wooden monoliths and fertility sculptures

name: Mon Town
description: District headquarters of Mon and gateway to Konyak Naga country in far northeastern Nagaland. Serves as base for exploring remote villages, cultural sites, and natural attractions along the Myanmar border; known for Aoleang festival and tribal markets.
facts: HQ of Mon district, home of Konyak Nagas
Elevation around 655 m
Base for Longwa, Shangnyu, Veda Peak visits
Aoleang festival held in early April
About 280 km from Dimapur

name: Veda Peak (Pak Koi)
description: Highest peak in Mon district, located about 70 km from the headquarters. Offers panoramic views of the Brahmaputra River (India) and Chindwin River (Myanmar) on clear days, plus a nearby waterfall. Historically the site of the first British camp and opium plantation in the Konyak hills.
facts: Highest point in Mon district
Views of Brahmaputra and Chindwin rivers
Nearby waterfall is a key attraction
About 70 km from Mon town
Site of first British camp in the area

name: Singphan Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Protected area of 23.57 km² in Mon district near the Assam border, notified in 2009 and declared Singphan Elephant Reserve in 2018. Supports Asian elephants, over 180 plant species, tropical forests, and serves as a critical corridor for elephant movement between Nagaland and Assam.
facts: Area 23.57 km², established 2009
Declared Elephant Reserve in 2018
Asian elephant corridor with Assam
Over 180 plant species
Near Assam border in Mon district

name: Chui Village
description: Traditional Konyak village near Mon known for morungs (men’s dormitories) decorated with animal skulls, horns, and tribal motifs. Offers authentic insight into Konyak warrior heritage, wooden architecture, and daily tribal life.
facts: Known for traditional morungs with skulls and horns
About 5 km from Mon town
Strong Konyak cultural architecture
Popular for cultural immersion
Part of core Mon tourism circuit

name: Chenloisho Village
description: One of the larger villages in the Chen area of Mon district, near the India-Myanmar border. Features a small museum of traditional Konyak ornaments, human skulls from headhunting era, and remote cultural experiences.
facts: Museum with traditional ornaments and skulls
Near India-Myanmar border in Chen area
One of the biggest villages in Chen region
Remote cultural and historical site
About 20 km from Mon town
